$comment: The family in 1910 — the private life behind the July Crisis chain's first link.

original.description: The family in a panelled salon with tall windows and gilt furniture. Franz Ferdinand sits at the left in a general officer's tunic with a newspaper on his knee; Sophie sits beside him in a high-necked dress and feathered hat; their younger son stands by a marble table with a flowering azalea; the elder son in a sailor suit leans against a grand piano at which their daughter is seated. The print carries a hand-lettered caption, 'Franz Ferdinand & Family, 1910.'
original.archive: Library of Congress, George Grantham Bain Collection — LCCN 2014697443, digital id ggbain.17181, glass negative
original.licence: public domain — Library of Congress: no known restrictions on publication; pre-1931

colorization.status: ok — label 'colorized (AI-assisted)'. Documented colours: the pike-grey Austro-Hungarian officer's tunic, dark blue sailor suits, gilt boiserie and parquet. The dress and upholstery colours are the colorizer's invention rather than a reading of anything documented, and the hand-lettered caption is part of the reproduction, not the original negative — both flagged for the image review (sand-y0u.7).

content_policy: ok — a family group, no gore; the children are named in the record and long dead
caption: Franz Ferdinand, Sophie and their three children at home in 1910. Their marriage was morganatic and their children barred from the throne; it was their fourteenth wedding anniversary that took them to Sarajevo on 28 June 1914. Colorized (AI-assisted) from a public-domain photograph.
credit: Original photograph: Bain News Service, 1910; Library of Congress, George Grantham Bain Collection (LCCN 2014697443, ggbain.17181); no known restrictions on publication. Colorization: Sandtable, AI-assisted, 2026.
notes: Supplied by Dave 2026-08-23 without a source. Matched to the Library of Congress Bain Collection record by title and year — the Commons copy of LCCN 2014697443 is titled 'Franz Ferdinand & family' and dated 1910, and this file's aspect ratio (1.387) is within cropping tolerance of the LoC negative's 1.369. The archive copy is a 5773 × 4216 glass-negative scan, so it is also the natural 'show original' target. Intended placement: the July Crisis chain and the Sarajevo backstory (sand-1l0.32).
